CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole benchmark):
- The binary is /workspace/executable (lz4 v1.10.0 CLI). You may ONLY run it and observe stdout/stderr/exit codes/output files.
- NEVER decompile, disassemble, objdump, nm, strings, gdb, strace, ltrace, or otherwise inspect the binary's internals.
- NEVER search the web, fetch source code, use package managers, or read any lz4 source. Do not install lz4.
- Only interact through the normal CLI interface.
- 'strings' and 'nm' on /workspace/executable are FORBIDDEN.

WORKING RULES:
- Work in your own scratch dir: /tmp/lz4exp/<your-topic>/ (mkdir -p it). Use ABSOLUTE paths everywhere.
- Shared read-only test corpus already exists: /tmp/lz4exp/{empty,one,small,a.txt,zeros64k,rand1m} and /workspace/assets/sample.txt.lz4
- Create your own extra test files as needed inside your scratch dir.
- 'xxd' is NOT installed; use 'od -A d -t x1' or python3 for hex dumps.
- Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY (e.g. cmd >out 2>err; echo $?) and record EXACT text including trailing spaces and newlines. Use 'od -c' when whitespace matters.
- Be exhaustive and systematic. Try edge cases, invalid inputs, weird combinations.
- Write your detailed findings to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/<topic>.md (mkdir -p /tmp/lz4exp/notes). Include verbatim transcripts.


YOUR TOPIC: test-mode
Write notes to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/test-mode.md

Probe TEST MODE (-t) of /workspace/executable.
Cover: -t on valid file; -t -v output text; -t on corrupted file; -t on non-lz4; -t with multiple files (-m); -t on stdin; -t combined with -d or -z; -t with output arg given; exit codes; whether -t writes any file; -t on legacy frames; -t on skippable-only file; -t on concatenated frames; -tv exact line format for each file; -t with --rm (does it delete?).

When done, RETURN a dense summary (<=120 lines) of the most important, exactly-reproducible facts a reimplementer needs. Include exact message strings in quotes. Do not include filler.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# TEST MODE (`-t`) — /workspace/executable (lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread)

All experiments in `/tmp/lz4exp/test-mode/probe/**`. stdout/stderr captured separately
(`1>o 2>e`) unless stated. All quoted strings are byte-exact (mind trailing spaces).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Flag forms

* `-t` short flag. Combinable in a cluster: `-tv`, `-tq`, `-tmc`, `-td`, ... all work.
* `--test` is an accepted **long form**, exactly equivalent to `-t` (undocumented in `-h`).
  - `--tes`, `--testx`, `--test=1` → exit 1, stderr `"Incorrect parameters\n"` + full usage.
* Repeating `-t -t` is harmless (exit 0, same output).

## 2. What -t does / does not do

* Fully decodes the stream, verifying frame header checksum, block checksums (if `-BX`),
  content checksum, and declared content size. Output is discarded.
* **Writes no file.** Verified: no output file created, `[output]` positional argument
  silently ignored, existing files with the derived name are NOT touched and no
  overwrite prompt is issued:
  ```
  $ ls                        # v_a.lz4 and pre-existing file "v_a"
  $ /workspace/executable -t v_a.lz4 ; echo $?   -> 0 ; "v_a" md5 unchanged
  $ /workspace/executable -t v_a.lz4 out.bin     -> 0 ; out.bin unchanged/not created
  ```
* Writes **nothing to stdout** in the plain single-file case (stdout length 0 always).
* Speed proves output is discarded: `-t` on a 307,200,000-byte frame finishes in 0.13 s.
* Compression-only options are accepted and ignored, but `-B4..-B7`/`-B<size>` still leak
  their compression message to stderr *before* the test output:
  `"using blocks of size 64 KB \n"`, `"... 256 KB \n"`, `"... 1024 KB \n"`, `"... 4096 KB \n"`.
  `-l -BD -BX --no-frame-crc --content-size --favor-decSpeed --fast -1 -12 --best -T4
  --sparse --no-sparse -f -k` produce no extra output.
* `-D FILE` **is honored** in test mode (see §8).

## 3. Success output — exact format

Single file, default verbosity (displayLevel 2), stderr:

```
b'\rDecompressed : 0 MiB  \r' + b' '*79 + b'\rv_a.lz4                        : decoded 135 bytes \n'
```

Decomposition (stderr only, stdout empty):
1. optional progress fragment `"\rDecompressed : %u MiB  "` (2 trailing spaces)
2. clear-line: `"\r"` + **79 spaces** + `"\r"`
3. final line: `"%-30.30s : decoded %llu bytes \n"`  (note space before `:` comes from the
   30-wide field, and there is a **trailing space** after `bytes`).

Field width proof (`n`-repeated names):
```
'n.lz4                          : decoded 135 bytes \n'      (52 bytes total)
'nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnn.lz4  : decoded 135 bytes \n'
'nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnn : decoded 135 bytes \n'      <- 34-char name truncated to 30
'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123 : decoded 135 bytes \n'      <- keeps first 30 chars
'/tmp/lz4exp/test-mode/probe/w/ : decoded 135 bytes \n'      <- path printed as given, truncated
```
Name shown is the *source* name exactly as typed; stdin shows as `stdin` (for `-`, `stdin`,
or no filename).

Progress fragment (step 1) is **omitted** when no LZ4F/legacy frame was actually decoded
(0-byte file, `/dev/null`, skippable-frames-only file, bare legacy magic):
```
$ -t empty.lz4    -> b'\r' + 79sp + b'\rempty.lz4                      : decoded 0 bytes \n'
```
Progress MiB value observed (deterministic per input on this machine, but it is a
time/buffer-throttled cosmetic counter — exactly ONE fragment ever appears, even for 300 MB):
`<2MB→0`, `2MB→1`, `3MB→2`, incompressible ≥4MiB→`3`, compressible ≥4MiB→`4`.

### Verbosity
| flags | stderr |
|---|---|
| `-t` | progress + clear + `decoded` line |
| `-tv` | `"*** lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread, by Yann Collet ***\n"` first, then as above |
| `-tvv` | banner + `"_POSIX_C_SOURCE defined: 200809L\n_POSIX_VERSION defined: 200809L\nPLATFORM_POSIX_VERSION defined: 200809L\n"` then as above |
| `-tvvv`, `-tvvvv` | identical to `-tvv` |
| `-tq`, `-tqq` | **completely empty stderr**, exit 0 |
| `-tvq` | same as `-t` (v and q cancel) |
Success output is 100% byte-stable (20/20 identical md5 for `-t v_a.lz4`).

## 4. Multiple files (`-m`) and recursion (`-r`)

* `-t -m f1 f2` → **empty stderr**, exit 0. The per-file `decoded` line requires `-v`
  in `-m`/`-r` mode (in `-m` mode the destination is stdout ⇒ message gated at level 3;
  `-tvv -m` prints `"Using stdout for output \n"` and
  `"Sparse File Support automatically disabled on stdout ; to force-enable it, add --sparse command \n"`).
  Same asymmetry exists for plain decompression: `-d -c f` is silent, `-dv -c f` prints the line.
* `-tv -m f1 f2` (exact):
  ```
  *** lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread, by Yann Collet ***\n
  \rDecompressed : 0 MiB  \r<79sp>\rv_a.lz4                        : decoded 135 bytes \n
  \r<79sp>\rv_small.lz4                    : decoded 36 bytes \n
  Done in 0.00 s ==> 0.22 MiB/s  (cpu load : 117%)\n
  ```
  The `Done in ... ==> X MiB/s  (cpu load : N%)` trailer is `-m`/`-r`-only, level ≥3, numbers vary.
* `-t -m` accepts files **without** the `.lz4` extension (plain `-d -m noext` refuses with
  `"File extension doesn't match expected LZ4_EXTENSION (.lz4); will not process file: noext\n"`, exit 1).
* `-t -r DIR` behaves like `-m` (names printed as `adir/v_a.lz4`), silent at level 2.
* Two positional args without `-m`: 2nd is the (ignored) output name — only file 1 is tested.
  Three positional args → exit 1,
  `"Error : v_one.lz4 won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n"`.
* `-t -m -` (only stdin) works but prints **no** `Done in` trailer.
* Error handling in `-m`:
  - a **corrupt** file is FATAL: processing aborts immediately, remaining files untested,
    exit = that file's error code (e.g. 34).
  - a **missing file** or a **directory** is only a warning: processing continues,
    final exit code is 1.
    `"nope.lz4: No such file or directory \n"`, `"lz4: sub2 is a directory -- ignored \n"`

## 5. `-c` interaction — IMPORTANT quirk

| command | stdout bytes | note |
|---|---|---|
| `-t f.lz4` / `-t -c f.lz4` / `-c -t f.lz4` / `-tc` / `-ct` | 0 | single-file: `-c` has no effect |
| `-t -m -c f1 f2` (any order: `-c -t -m`, `-mtc`, `-cmt`, …) | 171 = 135+36 | **decompressed data IS written to stdout** |
| `-t -r -c dir` | 171 | same |
| `--list -t f.lz4` | 135 | `-t` after `--list` also writes data to stdout |
| `-t --list f.lz4` | list table | `--list` wins: `"    Frames           Type Block  Compressed  Uncompressed    Ratio   Filename\n         1       LZ4Frame   B4I      154.00             -        -   v_a.lz4\n"` |
Integrity is still checked in those cases (`--list -t badhc.lz4` → exit 34); with
`-t -m -c good bad good` stdout gets the 135 bytes of the good file then aborts (exit 34).

## 6. `-d` / `-z` / `-b` interaction — LAST mode flag wins

```
-t -d v_a.lz4   -> real decompression: stderr "Decoding file v_a \n" + decoded line, CREATES file "v_a"
-d -t v_a.lz4   -> test only, no file
-t -z v_a.lz4   -> real compression: "Compressed filename will be : v_a.lz4.lz4 \n" ... CREATES v_a.lz4.lz4
-z -t v_a.lz4   -> test only
-t -d -z        -> compresses ;  -t -z -d -> decompresses (creates "v_a")
-t -d a.txt     -> exit 1, "Cannot determine an output filename \nIncorrect parameters\n" + usage
-t -b1 -i1 f    -> benchmark runs (stdout benchmark table), test skipped
```
Test mode never prints `"Decoding file X \n"` — useful discriminator.

## 7. `--rm` — YES, IT DELETES

```
$ -t --rm f1.lz4       -> exit 0, prints decoded line, f1.lz4 REMOVED
$ --rm -t f2.lz4       -> same (order irrelevant)
$ -t --rm bad.lz4      -> exit 34, bad.lz4 KEPT
$ -t --rm -m g1 g2     -> exit 0, both removed (silent)
$ -t --rm -m a1 BAD a3 -> exit 34; a1 removed, BAD+a3 kept (abort at BAD)
$ -t -k f              -> file kept (default)
```
Removal happens **before** the `decoded` message is printed:
```
$ /workspace/executable -t --rm - < v_a.lz4
exit 45
stderr: '\rDecompressed : 0 MiB  Error 45 : Remove error : stdin: No such file or directory \n'
```
i.e. with stdin it literally tries to `remove("stdin")` and no `decoded` line is printed.

## 8. Dictionary (`-D`)

```
$ lz4 -z -D a.txt a.txt dd2.lz4        (29 bytes)
$ -t dd2.lz4              -> 34  'Error 34 : Decompression error : ERROR_decompressionFailed \n'
$ -t -D a.txt dd2.lz4     -> 0   'dd2.lz4                        : decoded 135 bytes \n'
$ -t -D wrong.bin dd2.lz4 -> 34  'Error 34 : Decompression error : ERROR_contentChecksum_invalid \n'
```
A frame header carrying a dictID (flag+4 bytes, valid header checksum) is accepted with no
warning whether or not `-D` is given (exit 0).

## 9. Stdin

`-t`, `-t -`, `-t stdin`, `cat f | -t -`, `-t -m -` all work; display name is `stdin`.
Empty stdin (`< /dev/null`) → exit 0, `'stdin                          : decoded 0 bytes \n'`.
stdin is a TTY and no file given → exit 1, stderr `"refusing to read from a console\n"`.

## 10. Error catalogue (exit code + exact stderr line)

All error lines are `"Error %u : <msg> \n"` (trailing space before `\n`) and are printed with
`-q` but suppressed by `-qq`/`-qqq` (exit code unchanged).

| exit | stderr | trigger |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | (success line) | valid frame(s); 0-byte file; `/dev/null`; skippable-only file; 4-byte legacy magic only; skippable frame whose size runs past EOF |
| 1 | `nope.lz4: No such file or directory \n` | missing input |
| 1 | `lz4: adir is a directory -- ignored \n` | directory input (without `-r`) |
| 1 | `Stream followed by undecodable data at position 16 \n` + normal `decoded 0 bytes` line | junk after a *skippable* or *legacy* frame (position = byte offset) |
| 1 | `refusing to read from a console\n` | tty stdin |
| 1 | `Error : X won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n` | 3+ positionals, no `-m` |
| 26 | `Error 26 : LZ4F frame decoding could not complete: invalid frame \n` | truncated frame; missing endmark; magic-only (4 bytes); 1–7 bytes of trailing junk; duplicate endmark |
| 34 | `Error 34 : Decompression error : ERROR_headerChecksum_invalid \n` | corrupt FLG/BD/dictID or header checksum |
| 34 | `... ERROR_headerVersion_wrong \n` | FLG version bits ≠ 01 (checked *before* header checksum) |
| 34 | `... ERROR_reservedFlag_set \n` | FLG reserved bit set; BD block-size-id 0x80 |
| 34 | `... ERROR_maxBlockSize_invalid \n` | BD block-size-id 0; block size field > declared max (incl. 0x80000000 raw-block flag abuse) |

| 34 | `... ERROR_frameSize_wrong \n` | `--content-size` value ≠ actual decoded size |

| 42 | `Error 42 : Stream error : skippable size unreadable \n` | skippable magic + <4 bytes of size field |

Part (1) is **absent** when nothing was decoded: 0-byte file, `/dev/null`, skippable-only, bare legacy magic. Observed MiB value: `<2MB→0, 2MB→1, 3MB→2, incompressible≥4MiB→3, compressible≥4MiB→4`; exactly one fragment ever appears (even for 300 MB). Success output is byte-stable (20/20).

Verbosity: `-tv` prepends `"*** lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread, by Yann Collet ***\n"`; `-tvv` adds `"_POSIX_C_SOURCE defined: 200809L\n_POSIX_VERSION defined: 200809L\nPLATFORM_POSIX_VERSION defined: 200809L\n"`; `-tvvv`/`-tvvvv` same as `-tvv`; `-tq` and `-tqq` → **completely empty stderr**, exit 0.

## Writes nothing
No output file; the `[output]` positional is silently ignored (existing file untouched, no prompt); a pre-existing file with the derived name is not touched. 307 MB frame tested in 0.13 s. Compression opts ignored except `-B4..-B7`/`-B<size>` which leak `"using blocks of size 64 KB \n"` (also 256/1024/4096 KB) before the test output.

## `-m` / `-r`
- `-t -m f1 f2` → **empty stderr**, exit 0. The `decoded` line needs `-v` in `-m`/`-r` mode (dst is stdout there; `-tvv -m` prints `"Using stdout for output \n"` + `"Sparse File Support automatically disabled on stdout ; to force-enable it, add --sparse command \n"`). Same asymmetry as `-d -c` (silent) vs `-dv -c`.
- `-tv -m` prints one `decoded` line per file then `"Done in 0.00 s ==> 0.22 MiB/s  (cpu load : 117%)\n"` (level ≥3, `-m`/`-r` only, numbers vary). Absent when the only input is `-`.
- `-t -m` accepts non-`.lz4` names (plain `-d -m noext` refuses: `"File extension doesn't match expected LZ4_EXTENSION (.lz4); will not process file: noext\n"`, exit 1).
- Corrupt file in `-m` = **fatal, aborts**, later files untested, exit = its error code. Missing file / directory = warning only, continues, final exit 1.
- 2 positionals w/o `-m`: 2nd ignored, only file 1 tested. 3+ → exit 1 `"Error : v_one.lz4 won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n"`.

## `-c` quirk
`-t f` / `-t -c f` → 0 bytes stdout. But `-t -m -c f1 f2` (any flag order) **writes the decompressed data to stdout** (171 bytes) — same for `-t -r -c dir` and `--list -t f` (135 bytes). `-t --list f` → `--list` wins (table). Integrity still enforced (`--list -t badhc` → 34; `-t -m -c good bad good` emits 135 bytes then exits 34).

## Mode flags: LAST of {-t,-d,-z} wins
`-t -d f.lz4` **really decompresses and creates the file** (`"Decoding file v_a \n"`); `-d -t` = test only; `-t -z` really compresses to `v_a.lz4.lz4`; `-z -t` = test only; `-t -d -z`→compress, `-t -z -d`→decompress. `-t -d a.txt` → exit 1 `"Cannot determine an output filename \nIncorrect parameters\n"`+usage. `-t -b1` → benchmark runs instead. Test mode never prints `"Decoding file X \n"`.

## `--rm` DOES delete
`-t --rm f.lz4` → exit 0, prints `decoded` line, **source removed** (order irrelevant; also in `-m`). On failure the source is kept. In `-m` with a bad middle file, earlier successes are already deleted, the bad one and later ones are kept. Removal happens *before* the `decoded` line: `-t --rm - < f` → exit **45**, `'\rDecompressed : 0 MiB  Error 45 : Remove error : stdin: No such file or directory \n'` (no `decoded` line).

## `-D` honored
`-t dict-compressed.lz4` → 34 `ERROR_decompressionFailed`; `-t -D right` → 0; `-t -D wrong` → 34 `ERROR_contentChecksum_invalid`. A dictID in the header is accepted silently with or without `-D`.

## stdin
`-t`, `-t -`, `-t stdin`, pipes, `-t -m -` all work, name shown `stdin`. Empty stdin → exit 0 `decoded 0 bytes`. TTY stdin, no file → exit 1 `"refusing to read from a console\n"`.

## Accepted multi-frame shapes (exit 0, `decoded` = sum)
frame+frame = 171; frame×3 = 306; legacy+legacy = 270; **legacy then LZ4F = 270 (OK)** but **LZ4F then legacy = 34 `ERROR_frameType_unknown`**; skippable-only (`0x184D2A50`–`0x184D2A5F`, incl. empty payload) = 0; skippable+frame / frame+skippable / frame+skippable+frame = 135/135/171; skippable whose size overruns EOF = 0, exit 0.

## Non-determinism (important)
The progress fragment is emitted from a different thread than the error text, so on failure it may appear after, spliced into, or absent from the error output. Repeating `-t cat_bad2.lz4 2>e`: sizes 86,86,86,86,86,63. Forms seen: `'...invalid \n\rDecompressed : 0 MiB  '`, plain `'...invalid \n'`, and spliced `'Error 26 : LZ4F frame decoding could not complete: invalid frame\rDecompressed : 0 MiB   \n'`. Treat as cosmetic noise on error paths; success paths are stable.
